Anointment means the act of anointing — that is, the act of applying oil or a sacred liquid to a person (or sometimes an object) as part of a ceremony. But beyond the physical act of applying oil, anointment carries a much deeper meaning: it is a formal act that sets someone apart as specially chosen, blessed, or elevated above others.

Think of it this way: when you anoint someone, you are not just putting oil on them. You are marking them as someone special — someone selected for an important role, someone who now carries a kind of divine or official blessing.

1. The Literal, Ceremonial Meaning

In its most traditional sense, anointment refers to a religious or royal ceremony in which oil is applied to a person's head, hands, or body. This has been practiced for thousands of years across many cultures and religions.

In religion:

  • In Christianity, anointment is a sacred act performed by a priest or religious leader. It is used in rituals like the anointing of the sick (when a seriously ill person is blessed before death), baptism, and the ordination of priests.
  • In the Bible's Old Testament, kings and prophets were anointed with oil to signify that God had chosen them and given them authority. In fact, the word Messiah in Hebrew and Christ in Greek both literally mean "the anointed one" — a title given to someone whom God has specially chosen.
  • In Hinduism and several other traditions, anointing with oil or ghee (clarified butter) is part of various religious ceremonies too.

In royal coronations:

  • When a king or queen is crowned, one of the most sacred and central parts of the ceremony is their anointment. A religious leader pours or applies holy oil onto the monarch's head, hands, or chest. This act symbolizes that the ruler has received divine approval and blessing to govern.
  • This is not an ancient, dead tradition — King Charles III of the United Kingdom, for example, was anointed during his coronation in 2023, making it one of the most spiritually significant moments of the ceremony.

The key idea in all these literal uses: anointment marks a moment of divine or official blessing, and the person anointed is recognized as specially chosen or consecrated.

2. The Figurative Meaning (Everyday Modern Use)

Over time, the word anointment moved beyond religious and royal settings and entered everyday language with a broader, figurative meaning.

Today, when people use "anointment" outside a religious context, they mean:

The act of officially or informally choosing and designating someone as the successor, leader, or favored person for an important role.

This figurative use borrows the spirit of the original meaning — just as a king was anointed to signal "this is the chosen one," we now use anointment to describe situations where a powerful person or institution picks someone out and signals to the world that this is the person they have selected.

Examples of this figurative use:

  • "The retiring CEO's anointment of her deputy as successor came as a surprise to the board." (The CEO informally but clearly chose and designated her deputy as the next leader.)
  • "His anointment as the party's presidential candidate was made official at the national convention." (He was formally selected and declared the chosen candidate.)
  • "Many felt that the director's anointment of his own son as the next head of the studio was an act of nepotism." (He chose his son and elevated him to the position.)

Notice that in all these cases, no oil is involved — the word is being used metaphorically. But the feeling it carries is the same: someone is being specially selected and elevated, often by a person or group with authority.

Anointment is not a neutral word. It carries certain connotations (feelings and associations) that are important to understand:

  • Elevation: The anointed person is being lifted above others. They are not just selected from a list — they are set apart as special.
  • Authority and legitimacy: Anointment implies that the selection comes from someone with power or authority (God, a king, a CEO, a political party). It gives the chosen person a sense of legitimacy.
  • Solemnity: Whether used literally or figuratively, anointment has a serious, weighty tone. It is not a casual choice — it feels deliberate and significant.
  • Sometimes, criticism: In modern political or business language, "anointment" can carry a slightly negative or skeptical tone. When journalists write that a leader "anointed" their successor, they sometimes imply that the choice was made undemocratically — without consulting others, as if by royal decree. It can suggest that the chosen person received preferential treatment rather than earning the position through fair competition.
Common Contexts Where You'll See This Word

ContextWhat it refers to

You will encounter "anointment" most frequently in these areas:

  • Religious writing and scripture — referring to sacred rituals of blessing
  • Coverage of royal events — especially coronation ceremonies
  • Political journalism — when a party, faction, or powerful figure designates a preferred candidate or successor
  • Business reporting — when a senior leader openly designates the next person to lead an organization
  • Sports commentary — occasionally, when a young athlete is declared the "next great one" by coaches or the media ("his anointment as the heir to the throne of the sport")
A Few Example Sentences to Solidify Your Understanding

• "The priest performed the anointment of the dying man, offering prayers and applying sacred oil to his forehead."
  • "The anointment of King Solomon, as described in scripture, was a solemn ceremony that marked the beginning of his reign."
  • "Her anointment as the firm's managing partner came after fifteen years of dedicated work."
  • "Critics argued that the anointment of the chairman's nephew as director bypassed dozens of more qualified candidates."
  • "The young musician's anointment by the legendary producer opened every door in the industry for her."

Anointment is the act of applying sacred oil to a person as part of a ceremony (to bless, consecrate, or officially recognize them), or, in everyday figurative use, the act of choosing and designating someone as a specially selected person for an important role — always carrying a sense of elevation, authority, and deliberate selection.
